A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multimodal ego-trajectory prediction work, GEM dataset, and Path Complexity Index. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support comparison despite extensive renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original trajectory-prediction results on GEM and DR(eye)VE, loss and backbone ablations, and qualitative analyses in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results and additional attribution, modality-removal, gaze-noise, failure-case, and dataset analyses in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming G-MEMP to RouteFormer, v2 replaces convolution/pooling/fully connected scene-feature reduction with self-attention. Its architecture diagram and Appendix A.1 formulation also omit v1's separate motion encoder. Separate scene and gaze prediction targets and auxiliary losses become a fused visual-feature target with one auxiliary loss. Scheduled discounting becomes a fixed factor of 0.97. These revise key processing components and the training objective.

E1.justification: The GEM and DR(eye)VE datasets and ego-trajectory prediction task remain. v2 adds evaluation under missing input modalities and deliberately perturbed gaze positions in Appendices B.4 and C.4, extending sensor-input conditions without introducing another benchmark or newly collected population.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains the stationary and linear baselines, GIMO, and Multimodal Transformer. Appendix B.5 newly reports an adapted Autobots evaluation, with 10.87 m ADE on GEM. MTR is discussed but has no reported evaluation result, so it does not constitute another added evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v1 specifies PCI >= 20 selection; v2 reports both overall and 20+ PCI performance, and stated sampled training input increases from approximately 4 to 16 hours. Reported training changes include 250 to 200 epochs, 25 to 2 warm-up epochs, and learning rate 0.0005 to 0.00001. Informer model dimension changes from 128 to 832. The PCI-binned evaluation changes from DR(eye)VE to GEM. v2's eight-training-participant statement conflicts with Table 13's retained six-training/two-validation/two-test split, leaving the actual split revision unresolved.

E4.justification: The existing loss and backbone ablations remain, matched from v1 Tables 3-4 to v2 Tables 4-5. v2 adds prediction-horizon analysis, fixation attribution using Integrated Gradients, inference-time modality removal, gaze-noise robustness, and explicit failure cases. New traffic-content, GPS-noise, and urban PCI analyses also examine dataset characteristics and metric behavior. These substantially expand the questions tested beyond the original ablations and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for model performance. The new gaze-perturbation experiment tests measurement robustness rather than estimating result uncertainty. The GPS-distance distribution adds descriptive dataset analysis without specifying a new statistical inference or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially changes: v1 reports full-model ADE of 9.99/14.43 m on GEM/DR(eye)VE under its PCI-filtered protocol; v2 reports 7.70/12.26 m for 20+ PCI and 5.99/8.75 m overall. Changed training settings prevent treating these as controlled performance gains. The comparative FDE columns disappear, while horizon-specific FDE, attribution, modality-removal, gaze-noise, and dataset-statistic results are added. The original loss and backbone ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal auxiliary-loss definitions change from separate scene and gaze losses in v1 Appendix D to a loss on fused visual representations in v2 Appendix A.1. The PCI definition, ADE/FDE definitions, and basic discounted-error formula remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a multimodal prediction framework, PCI, and GEM, with state-of-the-art performance claims. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion now attribute benefits to driver field of view, explicitly comprising first-person video and gaze fixations. The earlier explicit claim of over 20% improvement on complex trajectories is removed.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations involving occluded turns, stopping or resuming at intersections, and multiple possible paths, with proposed remedies in Appendix B.3. It interprets missing-modality results for sensor availability, explains gaze-noise resilience through reliance on head-mounted video, and discusses input mismatch with multi-agent baselines. These substantially extend v1's predominantly positive interpretation of gaze benefits and successful trajectory examples.

D1.justification: v2 substantially revises the implementation configuration tables and newly documents median gaze downsampling and specific GIMO/Autobots adaptations. It supplies explicit access links for the declared open-source TORCHCACHE package and freely downloadable TRAJAPP utility. Conversely, v1's detailed GPS correction instructions, including piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation and annotation completeness checks, are omitted. Newly disclosed preprocessing details do not establish that those procedures changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands coverage of multi-agent prediction, language-model and human-inspired approaches, driver maneuver recognition, and eye-tracking research on attention, cognitive load, and fatigue. Added works include Autobots, MTR, GPT-Driver, and CEMFormer. Appendix B.5 also develops the distinction between driver-centric prediction and methods requiring multi-agent environmental inputs, materially expanding research positioning.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, methods and utilities are renamed, and the abstract, introduction, and related work are extensively rewritten. The main sequence changes from dataset/PCI/method to method/PCI/dataset. Appendices are reorganized around implementation, experiments, dataset, and PCI, with a contents list; references move before the appendices.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with redrawn framework diagrams and redesigned qualitative panels. Table 2 replaces ADE/FDE columns with overall and high-PCI ADE columns, and new tables and figures display attribution, robustness, failures, and dataset analyses. Existing material is also relocated: the sample driving sequence becomes Figure 8, the GPS interface becomes Figure 11, and the gaze montage is rotated in Figure 14.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central driver-attention contribution. v1 attributes benefits to gaze through comparisons that also remove the head-camera stream; v2 explicitly frames the contribution as field of view and adds fixation attribution, modality-removal, noise, horizon, and failure analyses. Quantitative dataset comparisons further substantiate GEM's motivation. These targeted gains outweigh reduced GPS-annotation detail and the new inconsistency between the stated training participant count and Table 13. Revised protocols still prevent interpreting lower scores as controlled performance gains.
